questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have a personal interest in South Korea, both culturally and historically.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Mixed. Certain things, like transportation and these were pretty easy to figure out and get information for. However stuff like banking and all of that, was a lot more complicated, due to the process in which ID's are done here

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Yonsei had a staffed area designated for international students regarding any problems and questions. This was very helpfull

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was only able to apply to live in one kind of Housing, SK Global house. Was enjoyable and I can recommend it if one is staying for one semester.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a cafeteria next to the dorms as well as a larger cafeteria, all within walking distance.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is more cramped then one might expect, in a good way, and as such one should be comfortable sharing a room with someone.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: One bids points on their website. It can be a bit tough, so look through the availability and such before the bidding goes live.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Didn't need any

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register as your major to ensure the best chance at getting the courses you need

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It varies. Some courses were a bit monotonous while others interesting and dynamic. Overall, if one chooses sufficiently hard courses, the academic level will be challenging

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Very different. No group classes, only lectures and video lectures. 
Prefer UCPH much more

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Public Finance
Game Theory and Applications
Economics of Energy and Environment
Sampling Theory in Data Science
International Political Economy
Korean 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Public Finance, Game Theory and Applications and Sampling theory in Data science.
These courses were challenging and interesting, while being in line with earlier material I had studied from UCPH.

questions.answer: Transportation quickly can become expensive if one is visiting a lot of sites. Get a climate card, which allows unlimited travel within Seoul.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: Usually not open to 1 semester foreign exchange students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different kinds

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore Seoul and get to know the city

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See all of the sites, such as Gyongbuk palace or Namsan tower. And utilise that Korea is relatively close to many other countries and flights are cheap.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fine

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Koreans can be hard to get to know, due to an overall language and cultural barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The respectfulness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. It will be expensive to do everything you want to do
2. Do some research before hand, especially with courses and stuff that you want to get done
3 It will be a very different learning experience, so be ready to adjust.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Basic stuff, do some research and prepare

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in another country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the everyday of a Korean University student.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: none

questions.answer: Yes
